Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

cruel adjective

also cruelty, cruelly, heartless, savage, fierce, ferocious

classical

Traupman 151
Lewis & Short: “morally rude or unfeeling … hard, unmerciful, cruel”
Traupman 299

crūdēlis, crūdēle

declension

cruel, hard-hearted

Other words

  • crūdēlitās, crūdēlitātis f. — cruelty

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 151; Lewis & Short: “in good prose and very freq.”; Traupman 299

    Lewis & Short: very frequent in good prose.

  • saevus, saeva, saevum — fierce, savage, raging; harsh, cruel

    declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 3.246: saevior leaena (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.18.13 (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 2.128 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Verg., Hor.)

    Roused to fierceness, where ferus is fierce by nature (Lewis & Short): of lions, boars and wolves, then of people, a harsh master or a stepmother.

  • saevitia, saevitiae f. — fierceness, savageness, cruelty

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.1: ad saevitiam ferae gignuntur (Lewis & Short); Tac. Ann. 6.19 (Lewis & Short)

  • saeviō, saevīre, saeviī, saevītum — be fierce, rage, vent one’s rage

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 10.1: saevīre Fortūna ac miscēre omnia coepit (Lewis & Short); Liv. 3.45: saevīre in tergum et in cervīcēs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sīcut avēs ad volātum, equī ad cursum, ad saevitiam ferae gignuntur

    as birds are born to fly and horses to run, and wild beasts to be savageQuint. 1.1.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • saevīre Fortūna ac miscēre omnia coepit

    Fortune began to rage and to throw everything into confusionSall. Cat. 10.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also callous.
